findings.title: Permission is bound to another ServiceAccount than the pod's
findings.cause: container loader exits because the API server refuses its ServiceAccount default: it may not list configmaps in namespace kd-rbac-other-serviceaccount. RoleBinding config-reader-read-configmaps grants it, through Role read-configmaps, to ServiceAccount config-reader, and the pod runs as ServiceAccount default (a pod whose template sets no serviceAccountName runs as default); its log says: "Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-other-serviceaccount:default\" cannot list resource \"configmaps\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kd-rbac-ot…"; Deployment settings-loader has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container loader exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 7 times
last lines of container loader's log (current run)
evidence.detail: Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:kd-rbac-other-serviceaccount:default" cannot list resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "kd-rbac-other-serviceaccount"

evidence.what: pod settings-loader-5f98f7849c-j8zql runs as ServiceAccount default
evidence.command: kubectl get pod settings-loader-5f98f7849c-j8zql -n kd-rbac-other-serviceaccount -o jsonpath='{.spec.serviceAccountName}'

evidence.what: Role read-configmaps, bound by RoleBinding config-reader-read-configmaps: apiGroups [""], resources ["configmaps"], verbs ["get", "list", "watch"]
evidence.command: kubectl get role read-configmaps -n kd-rbac-other-serviceaccount -o jsonpath='{.rules}'

evidence.what: RoleBinding config-reader-read-configmaps grants Role read-configmaps to ServiceAccount config-reader

findings.fix: Set serviceAccountName: config-reader in the pod template, or, if the app should keep ServiceAccount default, add it to the subjects of RoleBinding config-reader-read-configmaps.
